reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 with the 1989 Intrinsic Function amendment, every argument-1 of FUNCTION MEAN (identifier, literal, arithmetic expression, function, table ALL reference) must be of class numeric; an alphanumeric, alphabetic, numeric-edited, group, reference-modified or alphanumeric-function argument, or a nonnumeric literal, is refused.

edition-consulted.switches: sig.IntroducedIn > ctx.Edition.DialectLevel: MEAN's catalog row has IntroducedIn 85, so the function is available at --std 85

reader.edition-search: Read CheckArgumentClasses, the MEAN row of IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified (Uniform 'n', no predicates), Violation and Admissible('n' = class numeric by ByClass), and the class readers; grep for DialectLevel / Edition in IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs finds none on this path; MEAN's row has no edition-gated predicate.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the class-numeric screen is one path at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f37_02 exercises the rule at 1985; the refusals of numeric-edited, group, reference-modified, alphanumeric-function and figurative SPACE arguments are not exercised.

probes.printed: N -2.7500; ALL 4.0000 (a zero element included); EXPR 5.1250; FN 499999993.0000 (INTEGER(-12.5) with a COMP item); MAX18 9999999999999.0000 (a 14-digit item, cut to 13 integer digits by the probe's own editing picture); ZERO 0.0000
probes.expected: legal: signed, scaled, binary, table ALL, expressions, an integer function and zero; values are the arithmetic means (A.2.24.4)

probes.printed: error COBOL1627: FUNCTION MEAN argument-2 is of class alphanumeric; ISO §2023:15.3 requires class numeric
error COBOL1627: argument-1 is of class alphabetic
error COBOL1627: argument-1 is of class alphanumeric (numeric-edited)
probes.expected: refused: numeric-edited is class alphanumeric at 1985

probes.printed: error COBOL1627: argument-2 is of class alphanumeric ("5")
error COBOL1627: argument-1 is of class alphanumeric (group of one numeric item)
probes.expected: refused: a group is class alphanumeric

probes.printed: error COBOL1627: argument-1 is of class alphanumeric (WN2(1:2))
error COBOL1627: argument-1 is of class alphanumeric (CURRENT-DATE(1:4))
error COBOL1627: argument-2 is of class alphanumeric (UPPER-CASE(WX))

citations.check: OK  §1989:A.2.24.3 AR1  (2.24.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR1
OK  §1985:IV.4.3.3  (4.3.3 Concept of Classes of Data)  the text is in the clause

reader.notes: Conforms. Message text at --std 85 cites §2023:15.3 / §2023:15.60.3 r1, and the SPACE refusal names 'alphanumeric or national' although 1985 has no class national (message text only).
